statement: The Caliphate of Córdoba collapsed in the Fitna (civil war) of 1009–1031, fragmenting into approximately 23 Taifa kingdoms. The collapse followed a series of weak caliphs, the destruction of Medina Azahara by Berber mercenaries (1010), and the inability of any faction to maintain central authority. The Taifa kingdoms — often centered on individual cities — were militarily weak but culturally vibrant, producing the finest Arabic poetry and philosophy of the medieval period. Their weakness invited Christian military pressure (paying parias/tribute to Castile-León) and ultimately Almoravid intervention (1086).
